scope: Completed baseline and tighter-tolerance runs, both through 200 years. Numerical consistency and event comparison, not spatial convergence or exact reproduction.
early_prefix_agreement: Common100 and extended117 metrics exactly match the previously published audits.
report_prose:
The time-tolerance comparison also includes every resolved rupture over the first 100 years. The baseline and tighter-tolerance cases contain 20 and 20 resolved ruptures, respectively, from 21 and 20 complete threshold excursions.
The declared large-event criterion identifies 4 and 4 events, respectively.
Across the 20 chronological pairs, the maximum absolute differences are 83.2 min in onset, 1.47\% in duration, 1.1\% in peak speed, and 0.0062\% in maximum slip.
All pairs have identical connected 1 cm rupture footprints on the saved depth grid and identical large-event classifications.
These measurements test time tolerance on the baseline mesh. Footprint comparisons are limited by the saved depth spacing, about 30 m in the scientific runs. They do not establish spatial convergence or recovery of the published swarm sequence.

The baseline and tighter-tolerance runs both extend beyond the common validation window. We therefore repeat the comparison over their full shared duration of 200 years, so agreement confined to the early cycles cannot substitute for assessment of later events.
The time-tolerance comparison also includes every resolved rupture over the first 200 years. The baseline and tighter-tolerance cases contain 60 and 58 resolved ruptures, respectively, from 61 and 58 complete threshold excursions.
The declared large-event criterion identifies 7 and 6 events, respectively.
Across the 58 chronological pairs, the maximum absolute differences are 1.63e+07 min in onset, 718\% in duration, 743\% in peak speed, and 852\% in maximum slip.
Counts, saved rupture footprints, or large-event classifications differ between the catalogs; chronological pairing alone does not establish physical correspondence. The reported maxima compare ordinal catalog positions and cannot be interpreted as timing or amplitude errors between physically matched events.
These measurements test time tolerance on the baseline mesh. Footprint comparisons are limited by the saved depth spacing, about 30 m in the scientific runs. They do not establish spatial convergence or recovery of the published swarm sequence.

These long-duration catalog differences preclude claiming convergence of individual late events from this tolerance test. Early agreement does not certify the later figure cycles.
Large-event counts also depend on the declared span cutoff. With a 9 km cutoff, the baseline and tighter-tolerance catalogs contain 8 and 8 large events, compared with 7 and 6 at 10 km. All primary results retain 10 km; this relabeling does not remove differences in the resolved small-event sequences.
The fine-mesh and input-sensitivity runs do not cover this longer window. This additional temporal comparison therefore does not establish spatial convergence of the later figure cycles.
recomputation: python3 -c "import sys,json; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts'); from report_tables import tolerance_windows; b=json.load(open('data/baseline/analysis.json')); t=json.load(open('data/baseline_tight/analysis.json')); print(json.dumps(tolerance_windows(t,b,100.)[2],indent=2))"
scientific_findings: The raw audits pass for both 200-year calculations. Only the configured error tolerance changes, from 1e-5 to 2.5e-6; the source, executable, mesh and other parameters agree.
The 100- and 117-year event metrics exactly match the previously published stable-prefix audits.
The first differing saved footprint is ordinal 25 near year 117.645: the upper edge shifts by one saved depth interval, 30.517578125 m. Both events remain partial.

Over 200 years the catalogs contain 60 versus 58 resolved ruptures and seven versus six primary large events. The chronological-pair maxima compare different ordinal events after sequence changes and are not estimates of errors in physically matched events.

The baseline surface-reaching event near year 141.380 has a connected footprint at 0.01335--11.38496 km. A tighter-tolerance surface-reaching event near year 141.460 has a footprint at 0.01335--9.85146 km, falling below the primary 10 km criterion. These are illustrative catalog observations, not a formal one-to-one event assignment.

A 9 km span threshold yields eight large events in each run; 10 or 11 km yields seven and six. Primary panels retain 10 km. Event-label sensitivity does not remove the difference in resolved small-event counts.
The full tolerance test does not demonstrate convergence of individual late events. The fine-grid comparison covers only 100 years and cannot establish spatial convergence of the later figure cycles.
